Description: Run a list of child steps in order.

Parameters.Name: label

Parameters.Name: steps
Parameters.Label: Steps

Description: Run these steps without another exclusive macro sending input in between.

Parameters.Name: label
Parameters.Label: Name
Parameters.Hint: Optional label shown in the step list; leaving it empty shows the action's own name.

Parameters.Name: steps
Parameters.Label: Steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that send their keys and clicks as one run.

Description: Run these steps without another macro switching the page in between.

Parameters.Name: label
Parameters.Label: Name
Parameters.Hint: Optional label shown in the step list; leaving it empty shows the action's own name.

Parameters.Name: steps
Parameters.Label: Steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that work on the one page one after another.

Description: Wait a fixed amount of time before the next step runs.

Parameters.Name: ms
Parameters.Label: Wait
Parameters.Hint: How long to wait, in milliseconds; 1000 by default.

Description: Wait a random amount of time so the macro looks less mechanical.

Parameters.Name: minMs
Parameters.Label: Shortest wait
Parameters.Hint: Shortest wait, in milliseconds; 400 by default.

Parameters.Name: maxMs
Parameters.Label: Longest wait
Parameters.Hint: Longest wait, in milliseconds; 1200 by default, and no shorter than the shortest wait. Each run picks a number between the two and waits that long.

Description: Wait until a condition holds, then carry on.

Parameters.Name: condition
Parameters.Label: Condition
Parameters.Hint: Asked again and again until it holds. Any condition can be waited on: a colour, a picture, a piece of text, an element on screen, or a comparison between variables.

Parameters.Name: intervalMs
Parameters.Label: Check every
Parameters.Hint: How long to wait between two checks, in milliseconds: 200 by default, 0 to 60000, and an empty cell waits one screen refresh.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Waited ms
Returns.Hint: How long the wait actually lasted, in milliseconds.

Description: Run child steps a fixed number of times, for when you already know how many rounds it takes.

Parameters.Name: times
Parameters.Label: Times
Parameters.Hint: How many iterations to run, from 1 up; 10 by default.

Parameters.Name: intervalMs
Parameters.Label: Interval
Parameters.Hint: How long to wait between iterations, in milliseconds; 0 by default.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Body steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that run once per iteration.

Returns.Label: Why it ended
Returns.Hint: count when every round ran, break when the loop was left early.

Description: Repeat child steps while a condition stays true, for when only the state decides when to stop.

Parameters.Name: condition
Parameters.Label: Condition
Parameters.Hint: Checked before every iteration; the round runs only while it holds.

Parameters.Name: maxIterations
Parameters.Label: Max iterations
Parameters.Hint: Most rounds this loop runs, from 1 up; 1000 by default. Reaching it ends the loop rather than failing, which is what keeps a condition that never goes false from running on.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Body steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that run while the condition holds.

Returns.Label: Why it ended
Returns.Hint: condition when the condition became false, limit when the loop stopped at its maximum number of rounds, and break when it was left early with break.

Description: Run child steps once per item in a list or variable, for a batch of values that each want the same handling.

Parameters.Name: items
Parameters.Label: Items
Parameters.Hint: A list, or a $variable holding one. For example [1, 2, 3], split($text, ",") or $names.

Parameters.Name: itemVariable
Parameters.Label: Item variable
Parameters.Hint: Variable that receives the current item; item by default.

Parameters.Name: indexVariable
Parameters.Label: Index variable
Parameters.Hint: Optional variable that receives which round this is, counted from 0 in the order the items are walked in. Leave it empty to keep the round number out of the variables.

Parameters.Name: reverse
Parameters.Label: Reverse order
Parameters.Hint: Iterate from the last item to the first; off by default.

Parameters.Name: intervalMs
Parameters.Label: Interval
Parameters.Hint: How long to wait between rounds, in milliseconds; 0 by default.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Body steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that run once per item.

Returns.Label: Why it ended
Returns.Hint: items when the list ran out, break when the loop was left early.

Description: Count from one number to another, running the child steps each time, for when the steps need the number of the round they are on.

Parameters.Name: rangeFrom
Parameters.Label: From
Parameters.Hint: The first value the counter takes; 1 by default, and no less than -1000000.

Parameters.Name: rangeTo
Parameters.Label: To
Parameters.Hint: The last value the counter takes; 5 by default, and the value itself is included, so counting 1 to 3 runs three times.

Parameters.Name: stepSize
Parameters.Label: Step
Parameters.Hint: What the counter is increased by each round; 1 by default. A negative step counts down; 0 works the direction out from the two ends, counting down when From is above To.

Parameters.Name: intervalMs
Parameters.Label: Interval
Parameters.Hint: How long to wait between rounds, in milliseconds; 0 by default.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: Counter variable
Parameters.Hint: Variable that receives the value of this round; i by default, and the child steps can read it.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Body steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that run once per round.

Returns.Label: Why it ended
Returns.Hint: range when the counter reached its end, break when the loop was left early.

Description: Run one of two child blocks depending on a condition.

Parameters.Name: condition
Parameters.Label: Condition
Parameters.Hint: Checked once when the step runs: true runs the Then steps, false runs the Else steps.

Parameters.Name: then
Parameters.Label: Then steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps to run when the condition is true.

Parameters.Name: else
Parameters.Label: Else steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps to run when the condition is false.

Description: Run the one case whose values match, and the otherwise steps when none do.

Parameters.Name: switchValue
Parameters.Label: Value (operand)
Parameters.Hint: What the cases are compared against, read once when the step runs. Pick a variable from the list or type a name, a number or text of your own.

Parameters.Name: switchMode
Parameters.Label: Match mode (operator)
Parameters.Hint: How a case's values are compared with the value.

Parameters.Name: caseSensitive
Parameters.Label: Case sensitive
Parameters.Hint: Compare letter case exactly; off by default.

Parameters.Name: trim
Parameters.Label: Ignore spaces at the ends
Parameters.Hint: Drop the spaces at both ends before comparing. It changes "exactly" only; on by default.

Parameters.Name: multiline
Parameters.Label: Regex by line
Parameters.Hint: Let ^ and $ stand for the start and end of each line. It changes the regex comparison only; off by default.

Parameters.Name: cases
Parameters.Label: Cases
Parameters.Hint: One entry per case, tried from the top down. The first match runs and the rest are left alone.

Parameters.Name: otherwise
Parameters.Label: Otherwise steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps to run when no case matched.

Description: One branch of a switch: the values it answers to and the steps to run.

Parameters.Name: values
Parameters.Label: Values (operand)
Parameters.Hint: Values this case answers to, picked from the variable list or typed in, separated by ";". Each one is compared with the switch's value the way its match mode says.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Case steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that run when this case matches.

Description: Attempt some steps, handle a failure in another block, and always run a third.

Parameters.Name: body
Parameters.Label: Try steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps to attempt.

Parameters.Name: catchWhen
Parameters.Label: Catch only when
Parameters.Hint: Checked when the attempt fails. A variable field takes caught.key, an expression writes $caught.key, and $caught.detail holds the detail. Leave it empty to catch every failure; when the condition is false the original key and detail go to the caller.

Parameters.Name: catch
Parameters.Label: Catch steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps to run when the attempt fails.

Parameters.Name: finally
Parameters.Label: Finally steps
Parameters.Hint: Steps that always run, however it ended.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Error
Returns.Hint: The failure key the attempt ended with, or empty when it did not fail. Compare this value in a condition to branch on the reason.

Returns.Label: Error detail
Returns.Hint: What the engine was doing when the attempt failed, or empty when it did not fail or gave no more detail.

Description: Leave the innermost loop immediately.
Skip the rest of this iteration and start the next one.
End this macro now and carry on in the macro that called it. The results it has already set are handed back.
Hand the failure this catch block took on to the next level, keeping its key and detail unchanged.
Stop the running macro.

Parameters.Name: reason
Parameters.Label: Reason
Parameters.Hint: Optional note written to the log.

Description: Count this step as failed, so the failure rule written on it takes over.

Parameters.Name: reason
Parameters.Label: Reason
Parameters.Hint: What went wrong, written into the log and into the step's own error value so later steps can read it. Optional.

Description: Leave a line of explanation in the middle of a macro; running it does nothing.

Parameters.Name: note
Parameters.Label: Note
Parameters.Hint: What this part of the macro is for, written for whoever reads the macro next. It is taken as it stands: no variable is filled in, and nothing is written to the log.
Parameters.Placeholder: Set the export window up first.

Description: Store a value that later steps can read.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: Variable name
Parameters.Hint: Local variables are created here. Global variables must exist already; add them in the Variable Center.

Parameters.Name: scope
Parameters.Label: Scope
Parameters.Hint: Which layer the value goes in; local by default. Local values belong to this macro; global values are shared by every macro and must be created in the Variable Center first.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Label: Value
Parameters.Hint: The value to store: a number, text, a $variable, or a formula such as $count + 1 or upper($name).

Description: Work out an expression and store the answer in a variable.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: Variable name
Parameters.Hint: Where the answer is stored. Local variables are created here; global variables must exist already, add them in the Variable Center, and every macro shares them.

Parameters.Name: scope
Parameters.Label: Scope
Parameters.Hint: Which layer the value goes in; local by default. Local values belong to this macro; global values are shared by every macro and must be created in the Variable Center first.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Label: Expression
Parameters.Hint: A formula to work out, such as $count + 1, $total * 0.85 or concat($first, " ", $last). The expression editor writes it piece by piece.

Description: Add a number to a global variable as one step, so two macros adding at once do not lose an addition.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: Global variable
Parameters.Hint: The global variable to add to; it must already exist in the Variable Center. Every macro shares its value.

Parameters.Name: amount
Parameters.Label: Amount
Parameters.Hint: The number to add; it may be negative or a formula such as $step, and the default is 1.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: New count
Returns.Hint: The count after this step, so a condition or a later step can use it without reading the global again.

Description: Start a list variable, replacing whatever it held before.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: Variable name
Parameters.Hint: Local lists belong to this macro; global lists are shared by every macro. The name is created here for a local list; a global list must exist already, added in the Variable Center. Lists hold any mixture of values.

Parameters.Name: scope
Parameters.Label: Scope
Parameters.Hint: Which layer the list goes in; local by default. Local lists belong to this macro; global lists are shared by every macro and must be created in the Variable Center first.

Parameters.Name: items
Parameters.Label: Starting items
Parameters.Hint: What the list starts with, written as a list or a $variable; leaving it empty starts an empty list.

Description: Add one or more values to the end of a list.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: List variable
Parameters.Hint: The list to add to; the list offers the ones the macro can see.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Label: Value
Parameters.Hint: Value put at the end of the list; a variable or an expression may be used.

Description: Put a value into a list at a chosen position.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: List variable
Parameters.Hint: The list to insert into; the list offers the ones the macro can see.

Parameters.Name: listIndex
Parameters.Label: Index
Parameters.Hint: Position to insert at, counted from 0; 0 is the front. Write a position between 0 and the list's length; anything further out is taken as the nearest end.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Label: Value
Parameters.Hint: Value inserted at that position; whatever was there moves along one.

Description: Take the item at a chosen position out of a list.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: List variable
Parameters.Hint: The list to take something out of; the list offers the ones the macro can see.

Parameters.Name: listIndex
Parameters.Label: Index
Parameters.Hint: Position to remove, counted from 0; -1 removes the last item.

DisplayName: Change One Item Of A List
Description: Put another value in one position of a list, leaving the rest alone.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: List variable
Parameters.Hint: The list to change; the list offers the ones the macro can see.

Parameters.Name: listIndex
Parameters.Label: Index
Parameters.Hint: Position to change, counted from 0; -1 is the last item. A position the list has not got stops the step rather than quietly doing nothing.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Label: Value
Parameters.Hint: Value put at that position; the rest of the list is left alone.

Description: Empty a list without removing the variable itself.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Label: List variable
Parameters.Hint: The list to empty; the list offers the ones the macro can see. The variable itself stays, it is only what is inside it that goes.

Description: Write a message to the WhaleGenie log.

Parameters.Name: message
Parameters.Label: Message
Parameters.Hint: Text written to the log; it may run over several lines, and it may be a variable or an expression.

Parameters.Name: level
Parameters.Label: Level
Parameters.Hint: How the line is marked in the log; information by default.

Description: Ask a yes-or-no question and go on according to the answer.

Parameters.Name: message
Parameters.Label: Question
Parameters.Hint: The question, written in full. It is shown to whoever is at the machine while the macro waits for an answer.

Parameters.Name: detail
Parameters.Label: Detail
Parameters.Hint: Anything worth adding under the question, such as what the macro is about to do. Left empty, the question stands on its own.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Confirmed
Returns.Hint: True when the person said yes, false when they said no, and also false when there was nobody to ask, which is what a run a trigger started gets.

Description: Ask for a line of writing and keep it in a variable.

Parameters.Name: message
Parameters.Label: Question
Parameters.Hint: The question, written in full. It is shown to whoever is at the machine while the macro waits for an answer.

Parameters.Name: default
Parameters.Label: Answer box starts with
Parameters.Placeholder: What the answer box holds before the person types anything. It is only a starting point, and stands as the answer when they leave it alone.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Answer
Returns.Hint: What the person wrote. Empty when they cancelled, and when there was nobody to ask.

Description: Run another macro in this project and wait for it to finish. The called macro works on values of its own: this step fills in the arguments that macro declares, and asks for whichever of its results it wants.

Parameters.Name: macro
Parameters.Label: Macro
Parameters.Hint: Another macro in this project.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Description: Start another macro in this project in the background and keep a run handle for it. A later “Wait for a Background Run” waits for it and takes back the results this step asked for.

Parameters.Name: macro
Parameters.Label: Macro
Parameters.Hint: Another macro in this project.

Parameters.Name: runHandleName
Parameters.Label: Run handle
Parameters.Hint: The local variable the run handle goes into. Give the same variable to a wait, cancel or wait-all step later.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. The names are written once a “Wait for a Background Run” or “Wait for Every Background Run” step takes them back; until then they are not defined.

Returns.Label: Run handle
Returns.Hint: Where the background run is: its id, the macro it runs, whether it is running, the failure key if it failed, and the names of the results it will hand over.

Description: Wait for a macro started by “Start Another Macro”, then take back the results its start step asked for.

Parameters.Name: runHandle
Parameters.Label: Run handle
Parameters.Hint: The variable holding the handle that “Start Another Macro” wrote. Keep the handle in a variable that belongs to this macro; a handle can be waited for once.

Description: Look at a background run without waiting: whether it is still running, how it ended and why.

Parameters.Name: runHandle
Parameters.Label: Run handle
Parameters.Hint: The variable holding the handle that “Start Another Macro” wrote. The handle is brought up to date, so reading it later says what this step just learned.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the answers this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own.

Returns.Label: Status
Returns.Hint: running, done, failed or stopped: what the run is doing or how it ended.

Returns.Label: Still running
Returns.Hint: True while the run is still going; false once it has ended.

Returns.Label: Failure key
Returns.Hint: The run key it failed with, or empty when it did not fail.

Description: Cancel a background run and wait for it to stop, so what it was doing is no longer going on.

Parameters.Name: runHandle
Parameters.Label: Run handle
Parameters.Hint: The variable holding the handle that “Start Another Macro” wrote. The run is asked to stop and this step waits for it, so a run that cannot stop is reported rather than left behind.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Stopped
Returns.Hint: Whether the run ended because it was cancelled.

Description: Wait until every background run in a list is over, then take back the results each start step asked for.

Parameters.Name: runHandles
Parameters.Label: Run handles
Parameters.Hint: A list of run handles, for example a list built with “List Append” from handles that “Start Another Macro” wrote. Every run in it is waited for.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Waited
Returns.Hint: How many background runs this step waited for.

Description: Wait until one background run in a list is over, take back the results its start step asked for, and hand back which run it was.

Parameters.Name: runHandles
Parameters.Label: Run handles
Parameters.Hint: A list of run handles, for example a list built with “List Append” from handles that “Start Another Macro” wrote. The first run to finish is taken; the others keep running.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Finished run
Returns.Hint: The handle of the run that finished first, in its final state.

Returns.Label: Its place
Returns.Hint: Where that handle stood in the list, counting from one.

Description: Read a text file into a variable.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: File
Parameters.Hint: File to read. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Parameters.Name: storeAs
Parameters.Label: Store as
Parameters.Hint: Keep the file as one piece of text, or hand each line over as an item of a list, which is what walking through a file of names or paths wants. One piece of text is the default.

Parameters.Name: limit
Parameters.Label: Only the first
Parameters.Hint: Read only the first this many lines, from 0 to 1000000 and 0 by default. Zero reads the whole file, which a file of lines to pick a few out of does not want.

Parameters.Name: skipBlankLines
Parameters.Label: Leave out blank lines
Parameters.Hint: Drop the lines that hold nothing, so a blank line in the middle of a list of names does not become an item. Off by default.

Parameters.Name: trimLines
Parameters.Label: Trim each line
Parameters.Hint: Take the spaces off both ends of every line. Off by default.

Parameters.Name: encoding
Parameters.Label: Encoding
Parameters.Hint: How the file's text is turned into bytes. UTF-8 is what everything new uses and is the default; UTF-8 with a mark is what Notepad writes; GBK is what a Chinese Windows writes its own text files in; UTF-16 is what some older Windows programs expect. Reading follows the mark at the front of the file when it has one, and reads bytes that are not UTF-8 at all in this machine's own code page, which is how a CSV another machine exported still reads.

Returns.Label: Text
Returns.Hint: What the file held. With “one item per line” it is a list of lines.

Description: Write text to a file, replacing it or adding to the end.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: File
Parameters.Hint: File to write. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: fileContent
Parameters.Label: Text
Parameters.Hint: Text to write. Read as one value, so a variable or an expression may stand for it.

Parameters.Name: writeMode
Parameters.Label: Mode
Parameters.Hint: Replace the file, or add to what is already there. Replacing is the default.

Parameters.Name: newline
Parameters.Label: Line break
Parameters.Hint: Whether to put a line break around the text: none, one after it, or one in front of it when adding to a file whose last line never ended. None by default.
OptionLabels: In front of the text when it is needed

Parameters.Name: encoding
Parameters.Label: Encoding
Parameters.Hint: How the file's text is turned into bytes. UTF-8 is what everything new uses and is the default; UTF-8 with a mark is what Notepad writes; GBK is what a Chinese Windows writes its own text files in; UTF-16 is what some older Windows programs expect. Reading follows the mark at the front of the file when it has one, and reads bytes that are not UTF-8 at all in this machine's own code page, which is how a CSV another machine exported still reads.

Description: Add one line to a log file, creating the file when it is not there.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: File
Parameters.Hint: The log file the line is added to. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: logLine
Parameters.Label: Line
Parameters.Hint: What the line says. It is read as one value, so a variable or an expression may stand for it; a line break ends the line, and adding to a file whose last line never ended writes one in front of it.

Parameters.Name: timestamp
Parameters.Label: Put the time first
Parameters.Hint: Write the date and time in front of the line. On by default; a file of lines without them is hard to read afterwards.

Description: Check whether a file or folder is there.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: File
Parameters.Hint: File or folder to look for. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns
Parameters.Hint: Tick the results this step should hand over. Each ticked one becomes a variable of its own, named after the note on the step and the name of the result, which the row itself may change, and can then be read by later steps. Nothing ticked means the step leaves no result behind.

Returns.Label: Exists
Returns.Hint: True when the file or folder is there.

Description: Remove a file.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: File
Parameters.Hint: File to remove. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: toRecycleBin
Parameters.Label: To recycle bin
Parameters.Hint: Put the file in the recycle bin, where it can still be restored, instead of removing it for good. Off by default.

Description: Copy a file to another place.

Parameters.Name: from
Parameters.Label: From
Parameters.Hint: File to copy. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Label: To
Parameters.Hint: Where the copy goes. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: ifExists
Parameters.Label: If it is already there

Description: Move a file to another place, or rename it in the same folder.

Parameters.Name: from
Parameters.Label: From
Parameters.Hint: File to move. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: to
Parameters.Label: To
Parameters.Hint: Where it goes, name and all. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Name: ifExists
Parameters.Label: If it is already there
Parameters.Hint: What to do when a file of that name is already there: put this one over it, leave the one that is there alone, or give the new one a number of its own (report (2).csv). Putting this one over it is the default.
OptionLabels: Give the new one a number

Description: Make a folder, along with any folders above it that are missing.

Parameters.Name: path
Parameters.Label: Folder
Parameters.Hint: Folder to make. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Label: Path

Parameters.Label: Name
Parameters.Hint: The second half of a join. Only "join folder and name" uses it.

Parameters.Name: returns
Parameters.Label: Returns

Parameters.Hint: What the amount below is counted in; whole notches by default. Notches are the steps a wheel normally turns in. Pixels measure the same turn more finely, with 120 pixels to a notch; an application that only looks at whole notches may ignore the smaller amounts.

Parameters.Name: amount
Parameters.Label: Amount
Parameters.Hint: How far to scroll, counted in the unit above, from 1 up; 3 by default.

Parameters.Name: smoothMs
Parameters.Label: Smooth

Parameters.Name: x
Parameters.Label: X
Parameters.Hint: The column of the place to scroll at, counted from the coordinate origin above, in pixels; 0 by default. Nothing is written here while the place comes from the pointer.

Parameters.Name: y
Parameters.Label: Y
Parameters.Hint: The row of the place to scroll at, counted from the same origin and in the same pixels; 0 by default.

Parameters.Name: useCursor
Parameters.Label: At the pointer's place
Parameters.Hint: With this on the step writes no coordinates and works wherever the pointer is at the time. Use it when the place is decided by where the user left the mouse; the X and Y fields are then not written and not read.

Parameters.Name: place
Parameters.Label: Place
Parameters.Hint: A record whose x and y say where, such as a hit, a window or a picture taken earlier; its x and y are the middle of what it names. Fill this in to scroll where an earlier step found something, instead of writing the two numbers.

Parameters.Name: anchorMode

Description: Look for a reference image on screen.

Parameters.Label: Reference pictures

Parameters.Name: confidence
Parameters.Label: Confidence %
Parameters.Hint: How alike the picture on screen has to be, from 0 to 100 per cent; the default is 90. Raise it to accept fewer false matches, lower it when the screen is drawn a little differently.

Parameters.Name: imageSet
Parameters.Label: Which of the pictures
Parameters.Hint: Which of the pictures above this step goes with. The first that turns up, the default, is what a button drawn two ways asks for. The surest of them looks at every picture and takes the one whose closest match scored highest, which is how the closer of two similar icons is picked. Every one of them asks for the whole set at once, so a step acts only on a screen showing all of them and finds nothing when one is missing; where a match is handed over it is the first picture's, and the hit that is handed over is counted inside that picture as usual.

Parameters.Name: detectAlgorithm
Parameters.Label: Recognition algorithm
Parameters.Hint: How the reference picture is recognised. Normalised, the default, takes the brightness out first, so an area that has gone brighter or darker still matches. Correlated does not, which is steadier for a very small picture. Pixel for pixel wants a copy, which a flat icon or a screenshot of a dialog is. Features pairs up what stands out in both pictures, so it still finds the thing at another size: slower, and it reports a single hit.

Parameters.Name: ignoreColor
Parameters.Label: Colour to ignore
Parameters.Hint: Pixels of the reference picture that are this colour take no part in the comparing. For a part of the picture that keeps changing, such as a number over a button or a progress bar. Empty compares the whole picture, which is the default.

Parameters.Name: minFeatures
Parameters.Label: Least feature pairs
Parameters.Hint: Only used when the algorithm is features: how many pairs have to line up before the picture counts as found. From 1 to 500, more is stricter; the default is 6.

Parameters.Name: orderBy
Parameters.Label: Count them in
Parameters.Hint: What order the hits are numbered in, which is what the match number counts. Reading, the default, is down the screen first and then across. Score takes the surest one wherever it is. Description: Look for a colour that has the colours this step names around it, which is how two things drawn alike are told apart.

Parameters.Label: Base colour

Parameters.Name: region

Parameters.Name: caseSensitive

Parameters.Name: multiline

Parameters.Name: sendsInput
Parameters.Label: The script sends keyboard or mouse input
Parameters.Hint: Turn this on when the script types or clicks by itself. It is a declaration for the design-time warning: WhaleGenie cannot see input a script sends directly, so the input door cannot hold it back. Off by default.

Parameters.Name: kind
Parameters.Label: Kind of script
Parameters.Hint: What this step hands the script to. The three command kinds write the text out as a batch file and run it with cmd.exe: the first one leaves its window open afterwards so what it printed can be read, the second closes the window when the command is done, and the third shows no window at all. The two file kinds and the PowerShell and AutoHotkey kinds run without a window; a program of your own choosing is for anything else the machine has. PowerShell by default.
OptionLabels: CMD command (close the window after it)

Parameters.Name: encoding
Parameters.Label: Script file encoding
Parameters.Hint: How the copy of the script handed to the program is written. Left to decide for itself, a batch file or a command gets this machine's own code page, PowerShell and AutoHotkey get a byte-order mark, and a program of your own choosing gets plain UTF-8, which is what each of them reads correctly. A program that reads the system code page instead, cscript for one, needs GBK to read Chinese text. Reading it as the kind of script expects is the default.
OptionLabels: As this kind of script expects

Parameters.Name: scriptSource
Parameters.Label: Run
Parameters.Hint: What this step runs: the script written below, or a file that is already on this machine. A file is run where it lies, so what it reads beside itself, what it includes and what its own folder is all stay what its author wrote, and nothing takes the place of {{name}} in it. The script written below by default.

Parameters.Name: script
Parameters.Label: Script
Parameters.Hint: The script itself, told to the program named above. {{name}} is replaced by what the variable name holds before the script runs, which is how a macro value gets in; everything the script prints comes back in the output result where the kind of script can be read that way.

Parameters.Name: scriptFile
Parameters.Label: Script file
Parameters.Hint: The script to run, named where it stands; the kind of script above is what runs it, and the file's own ending is not looked at. Point this at a script somebody else keeps up to date, or one too long to keep in a step. A path on its own is taken to be inside the macros folder.

Parameters.Label: Arguments

Description: True when a reference image is on screen.

Parameters.Name: images
Parameters.Label: Reference pictures
Parameters.Hint: The pictures to look for, one row each, tried in the order they are listed; the condition is true as soon as one of them turns up.

Parameters.Name: imageSet
Parameters.Label: Which of the pictures
Parameters.Hint: Which of the pictures above this step goes with. The first that turns up, the default, is what a button drawn two ways asks for. The surest of them looks at every picture and takes the one whose closest match scored highest, which is how the closer of two similar icons is picked. Every one of them asks for the whole set at once, so a step acts only on a screen showing all of them and finds nothing when one is missing; where a match is handed over it is the first picture's, and the hit that is handed over is counted inside that picture as usual.

Parameters.Name: confidence
Parameters.Label: Confidence %
Parameters.Hint: The lowest match confidence that still counts as found, as a whole percent from 0 to 100; 90 by default. Lower it for a reference picture that is drawn a little differently each time.

Parameters.Name: region
Parameters.Label: Search region
Parameters.Hint: Where to look: one row per place, and there may be several. A row is x, y, width and height, dragged out with “pick region” or typed in; a row may also name a variable, either one holding a picture an earlier Capture took, which is searched inside, or one holding a rectangle written as x,y,width,height, or a record carrying one (a hit, a window, an element). A record's numbers are where it is on the screen, so the coordinate origin moves the four numbers written out and not a record. Empty searches the whole screen, which is the default.

Parameters.Name: frameMaxAgeMs
Parameters.Label: Accept a picture up to
Parameters.Hint: How old a picture this step will accept, in milliseconds, from 0 to 60000; the default is 0, which reads the screen every time. A step that allows a picture taken within the last few milliseconds is handed one an earlier step took of the same window, or of the screen, so looking at the same place again and again does not read it again and again. The first reading with this allowed takes the whole window or the whole screen, which is what the readings after it save.

Parameters.Name: intervalMs
Parameters.Label: Interval
Parameters.Hint: The least time this step leaves between two looks at the screen, in milliseconds, from 0 to 60000; the default is 0, which looks again as soon as the step is asked to. Writing a gap is worth it when the step sits inside a loop, where a step that reads the same place on every pass spends most of its time reading a picture that has not changed. Seven milliseconds is about 144 looks a second.

Parameters.Name: anchorMode
Parameters.Label: Coordinates from
Parameters.Hint: What this step's coordinates are measured from. Screen is a pixel position on the desktop, which is how macros were written before this setting existed. Window and client measure from the window named below instead, so the step lands in the same place inside that window after it has been moved or resized. Element measures from a control, found by the selector below, so the numbers follow that control around the screen and through a list that scrolls.

Parameters.Name: anchorWindow
Parameters.Label: Match text
Parameters.Hint: The text the window is recognised by, held up against its title, the program that owns it or the class it registered, the way "Match by" says, ignoring case. The pixels this step reads come out of that window. Leave it empty for the window in front.

Parameters.Name: anchorHow
Parameters.Label: Match by
Parameters.Hint: How the window is recognised: the text is held up against the window's title, or against the name of the program that owns it or the class that program registered. Contained in it and exactly it are the two that work on all three; a title can also be held up to its start or its end, or matched as a regular expression. The screen and element origins do not use it.

Parameters.Name: caseSensitive
Parameters.Label: Case sensitive
Parameters.Hint: Compare letter case exactly; off by default.

Parameters.Name: trim
Parameters.Label: Ignore spaces at the ends
Parameters.Hint: Drop the spaces at both ends before comparing. It changes "exactly" only; on by default.

Parameters.Name: multiline
Parameters.Label: Regex by line
Parameters.Hint: Let ^ and $ stand for the start and end of each line. It changes the regex comparison only; off by default.

Description: True when an element of the page is in the state named.

Parameters.Name: pageSelector
Parameters.Label: Selector
Parameters.Hint: One selector to a line: they are tried in that order, and the first that finds the element is the one this step uses, so a second line is what keeps a step working after the page has been redesigned. A later line is reached only when the one before it finds nothing at all, not when it finds an element that will not be acted on. A $variable written in a line is filled in with its value.
